work.title: The First Part of Henry the Sixth
work.author: William Shakespeare

content.text: Sound a Flourish. Enter Charles, Alençon and Reignier, marching with Drum and Soldiers.

lines.text: Mars his true moving, even as in the heavens
lines.plainText: Mars his true moving even as in the heavens

lines.text: So in the earth, to this day is not known.
lines.plainText: So in the earth to this day is not known

lines.text: Late did he shine upon the English side;
lines.plainText: Late did he shine upon the English side

lines.text: Now we are victors; upon us he smiles.
lines.plainText: Now we are victors upon us he smiles

lines.text: What towns of any moment but we have?
lines.plainText: What towns of any moment but we have

lines.text: At pleasure here we lie near Orleans,
lines.plainText: At pleasure here we lie near Orleans

lines.text: Otherwhiles the famish'd English, like pale ghosts,
lines.plainText: Otherwhiles the famish'd English like pale ghosts

lines.text: Faintly besiege us one hour in a month.
lines.plainText: Faintly besiege us one hour in a month

lines.text: Let's raise the siege. Why live we idly here?
lines.plainText: Let's raise the siege Why live we idly here

lines.text: Talbot is taken, whom we wont to fear.
lines.plainText: Talbot is taken whom we wont to fear

lines.text: Remaineth none but mad-brain'd Salisbury,
lines.plainText: Remaineth none but madbrain'd Salisbury

lines.text: And he may well in fretting spend his gall;
lines.plainText: And he may well in fretting spend his gall

lines.text: Nor men nor money hath he to make war.
lines.plainText: Nor men nor money hath he to make war

lines.text: Sound, sound alarum! We will rush on them.
lines.plainText: Sound sound alarum We will rush on them

lines.text: Now for the honour of the forlorn French!
lines.plainText: Now for the honour of the forlorn French

lines.text: Him I forgive my death that killeth me
lines.plainText: Him I forgive my death that killeth me

lines.text: When he sees me go back one foot or fly.
lines.plainText: When he sees me go back one foot or fly

content.text: Here alarum; they are beaten back by the English, with great loss. Re-enter Charles, Alençon and Reignier.

lines.text: Who ever saw the like? What men have I!
lines.plainText: Who ever saw the like What men have I

lines.text: Dogs, cowards, dastards! I would ne'er have fled
lines.plainText: Dogs cowards dastards I would ne'er have fled

lines.text: But that they left me 'midst my enemies.
lines.plainText: But that they left me 'midst my enemies

lines.text: Salisbury is a desperate homicide;
lines.plainText: Salisbury is a desperate homicide

lines.text: He fighteth as one weary of his life.
lines.plainText: He fighteth as one weary of his life

lines.text: The other lords, like lions wanting food,
lines.plainText: The other lords like lions wanting food

lines.text: Do rush upon us as their hungry prey.
lines.plainText: Do rush upon us as their hungry prey

lines.text: Let's leave this town; for they are hare-brain'd slaves,
lines.plainText: Let's leave this town for they are harebrain'd slaves

lines.text: And hunger will enforce them to be more eager.
lines.plainText: And hunger will enforce them to be more eager

lines.text: Of old I know them; rather with their teeth
lines.plainText: Of old I know them rather with their teeth

lines.text: The walls they'll tear down than forsake the siege.
lines.plainText: The walls they'll tear down than forsake the siege

lines.text: I think by some odd gimmers or device
lines.plainText: I think by some odd gimmers or device

lines.text: Their arms are set like clocks, still to strike on;
lines.plainText: Their arms are set like clocks still to strike on

lines.text: Else ne'er could they hold out so as they do.
lines.plainText: Else ne'er could they hold out so as they do

lines.text: By my consent, we'll even let them alone.
lines.plainText: By my consent we'll even let them alone

lines.text: Where's the Prince Dauphin? I have news for him.
lines.plainText: Where's the Prince Dauphin I have news for him

lines.text: Bastard of Orleans, thrice welcome to us.
lines.plainText: Bastard of Orleans thrice welcome to us

lines.text: Methinks your looks are sad, your cheer appall'd.
lines.plainText: Methinks your looks are sad your cheer appall'd

lines.text: Hath the late overthrow wrought this offence?
lines.plainText: Hath the late overthrow wrought this offence

lines.text: Be not dismay'd, for succour is at hand.
lines.plainText: Be not dismay'd for succour is at hand

lines.text: A holy maid hither with me I bring,
lines.plainText: A holy maid hither with me I bring

lines.text: Which, by a vision sent to her from heaven
lines.plainText: Which by a vision sent to her from heaven

lines.text: Ordained is to raise this tedious siege
lines.plainText: Ordained is to raise this tedious siege

lines.text: And drive the English forth the bounds of France.
lines.plainText: And drive the English forth the bounds of France

lines.text: The spirit of deep prophecy she hath,
lines.plainText: The spirit of deep prophecy she hath

lines.text: Exceeding the nine sibyls of old Rome.
lines.plainText: Exceeding the nine sibyls of old Rome

lines.text: What's past and what's to come she can descry.
lines.plainText: What's past and what's to come she can descry

lines.text: Speak, shall I call her in? Believe my words,
lines.plainText: Speak shall I call her in Believe my words

lines.text: For they are certain and unfallible.
lines.plainText: For they are certain and unfallible

lines.text: Go, call her in.
lines.plainText: Go call her in

content.text: Re-enter the Bastard of Orleans, with Joan la Pucelle.

lines.text: Fair maid, is 't thou wilt do these wondrous feats?
lines.plainText: Fair maid is 't thou wilt do these wondrous feats

lines.text: Reignier is 't thou that thinkest to beguile me?
lines.plainText: Reignier is 't thou that thinkest to beguile me

lines.text: Where is the Dauphin? Come, come from behind;
lines.plainText: Where is the Dauphin Come come from behind

lines.text: I know thee well, though never seen before.
lines.plainText: I know thee well though never seen before

lines.text: Be not amazed, there's nothing hid from me.
lines.plainText: Be not amazed there's nothing hid from me

lines.text: In private will I talk with thee apart.
lines.plainText: In private will I talk with thee apart

lines.text: Stand back, you lords, and give us leave awhile.
lines.plainText: Stand back you lords and give us leave awhile

lines.text: She takes upon her bravely at first dash.
lines.plainText: She takes upon her bravely at first dash

lines.text: Dauphin, I am by birth a shepherd's daughter,
lines.plainText: Dauphin I am by birth a shepherd's daughter

lines.text: My wit untrain'd in any kind of art.
lines.plainText: My wit untrain'd in any kind of art

lines.text: Heaven and our Lady gracious hath it pleased
lines.plainText: Heaven and our Lady gracious hath it pleased

lines.text: To shine on my contemptible estate.
lines.plainText: To shine on my contemptible estate

lines.text: Lo, whilst I waited on my tender lambs,
lines.plainText: Lo whilst I waited on my tender lambs

lines.text: And to sun's parching heat display'd my cheeks,
lines.plainText: And to sun's parching heat display'd my cheeks

lines.text: God's mother deigned to appear to me,
lines.plainText: God's mother deigned to appear to me

lines.text: And in a vision full of majesty
lines.plainText: And in a vision full of majesty

lines.text: Will'd me to leave my base vocation
lines.plainText: Will'd me to leave my base vocation

lines.text: And free my country from calamity.
lines.plainText: And free my country from calamity

lines.text: Her aid she promised and assured success.
lines.plainText: Her aid she promised and assured success

lines.text: In complete glory she reveal'd herself;
lines.plainText: In complete glory she reveal'd herself

lines.text: And, whereas I was black and swart before,
lines.plainText: And whereas I was black and swart before

lines.text: With those clear rays which she infused on me
lines.plainText: With those clear rays which she infused on me

lines.text: That beauty am I blest with which you may see.
lines.plainText: That beauty am I blest with which you may see

lines.text: Ask me what question thou canst possible,
lines.plainText: Ask me what question thou canst possible

lines.text: And I will answer unpremeditated.
lines.plainText: And I will answer unpremeditated

lines.text: My courage try by combat, if thou dar'st,
lines.plainText: My courage try by combat if thou dar'st

lines.text: And thou shalt find that I exceed my sex.
lines.plainText: And thou shalt find that I exceed my sex

lines.text: Resolve on this; thou shalt be fortunate
lines.plainText: Resolve on this thou shalt be fortunate

lines.text: If thou receive me for thy warlike mate.
lines.plainText: If thou receive me for thy warlike mate

lines.text: Thou hast astonish'd me with thy high terms.
lines.plainText: Thou hast astonish'd me with thy high terms

lines.text: Only this proof I'll of thy valour make:
lines.plainText: Only this proof I'll of thy valour make

lines.text: In single combat thou shalt buckle with me,
lines.plainText: In single combat thou shalt buckle with me

lines.text: And if thou vanquishest, thy words are true;
lines.plainText: And if thou vanquishest thy words are true

lines.text: Otherwise I renounce all confidence.
lines.plainText: Otherwise I renounce all confidence

lines.text: I am prepared. Here is my keen-edg'd sword,
lines.plainText: I am prepared Here is my keenedg'd sword

lines.text: Deck'd with five flower-de-luces on each side,
lines.plainText: Deck'd with five flowerdeluces on each side

lines.text: The which at Touraine, in Saint Katharine's churchyard,
lines.plainText: The which at Touraine in Saint Katharine's churchyard

lines.text: Out of a great deal of old iron I chose forth.
lines.plainText: Out of a great deal of old iron I chose forth

lines.text: Then come, o' God's name; I fear no woman.
lines.plainText: Then come o' God's name I fear no woman

lines.text: And while I live, I'll ne'er fly from a man.
lines.plainText: And while I live I'll ne'er fly from a man

content.text: [Here they fight, and Joan la Pucelle overcomes.]

lines.text: Stay, stay thy hands; thou art an Amazon,
lines.plainText: Stay stay thy hands thou art an Amazon

lines.text: And fightest with the sword of Deborah.
lines.plainText: And fightest with the sword of Deborah

lines.text: Christ's Mother helps me, else I were too weak.
lines.plainText: Christ's Mother helps me else I were too weak

lines.text: Whoe'er helps thee, 'tis thou that must help me.
lines.plainText: Whoe'er helps thee 'tis thou that must help me

lines.text: Impatiently I burn with thy desire;
lines.plainText: Impatiently I burn with thy desire

lines.text: My heart and hands thou hast at once subdued.
lines.plainText: My heart and hands thou hast at once subdued

lines.text: Excellent Pucelle, if thy name be so,
lines.plainText: Excellent Pucelle if thy name be so

lines.text: Let me thy servant and not sovereign be.
lines.plainText: Let me thy servant and not sovereign be

lines.text: 'Tis the French Dauphin sueth to thee thus.
lines.plainText: 'Tis the French Dauphin sueth to thee thus

lines.text: I must not yield to any rites of love,
lines.plainText: I must not yield to any rites of love

lines.text: For my profession's sacred from above.
lines.plainText: For my profession's sacred from above

lines.text: When I have chased all thy foes from hence,
lines.plainText: When I have chased all thy foes from hence

lines.text: Then will I think upon a recompense.
lines.plainText: Then will I think upon a recompense

lines.text: Meantime look gracious on thy prostrate thrall.
lines.plainText: Meantime look gracious on thy prostrate thrall

lines.text: My lord, methinks, is very long in talk.
lines.plainText: My lord methinks is very long in talk

lines.text: Shall we disturb him, since he keeps no mean?
lines.plainText: Shall we disturb him since he keeps no mean

lines.text: My lord, where are you? What devise you on?
lines.plainText: My lord where are you What devise you on

lines.text: Shall we give over Orleans, or no?
lines.plainText: Shall we give over Orleans or no

lines.text: Why, no, I say. Distrustful recreants!
lines.plainText: Why no I say Distrustful recreants

lines.text: Fight till the last gasp; I will be your guard.
lines.plainText: Fight till the last gasp I will be your guard

lines.text: What she says I'll confirm. We'll fight it out.
lines.plainText: What she says I'll confirm We'll fight it out

lines.text: Assign'd am I to be the English scourge.
lines.plainText: Assign'd am I to be the English scourge

lines.text: This night the siege assuredly I'll raise.
lines.plainText: This night the siege assuredly I'll raise

lines.text: Expect Saint Martin's summer, halcyon's days,
lines.plainText: Expect Saint Martin's summer halcyon's days

lines.text: Since I have entered into these wars.
lines.plainText: Since I have entered into these wars

lines.text: Glory is like a circle in the water,
lines.plainText: Glory is like a circle in the water

lines.text: Which never ceaseth to enlarge itself
lines.plainText: Which never ceaseth to enlarge itself

lines.text: Till by broad spreading it disperse to nought.
lines.plainText: Till by broad spreading it disperse to nought

lines.text: With Henry's death the English circle ends;
lines.plainText: With Henry's death the English circle ends

lines.text: Dispersed are the glories it included.
lines.plainText: Dispersed are the glories it included

lines.text: Now am I like that proud insulting ship
lines.plainText: Now am I like that proud insulting ship

lines.text: Which Caesar and his fortune bare at once.
lines.plainText: Which Caesar and his fortune bare at once

lines.text: Was Mahomet inspired with a dove?
lines.plainText: Was Mahomet inspired with a dove

lines.text: Thou with an eagle art inspired then.
lines.plainText: Thou with an eagle art inspired then

lines.text: Helen, the mother of great Constantine,
lines.plainText: Helen the mother of great Constantine

lines.text: Nor yet Saint Philip's daughters, were like thee.
lines.plainText: Nor yet Saint Philip's daughters were like thee

lines.text: Bright star of Venus, fall'n down on the earth,
lines.plainText: Bright star of Venus fall'n down on the earth

lines.text: How may I reverently worship thee enough?
lines.plainText: How may I reverently worship thee enough

lines.text: Woman, do what thou canst to save our honours;
lines.plainText: Woman do what thou canst to save our honours

lines.text: Drive them from Orleans and be immortalized.
lines.plainText: Drive them from Orleans and be immortalized

lines.text: Presently we'll try. Come, let's away about it.
lines.plainText: Presently we'll try Come let's away about it

lines.text: No prophet will I trust if she prove false.
lines.plainText: No prophet will I trust if she prove false
